===========================
RUNNING ORBIXERP DAY TO DAY
===========================

  On Windows the simplest way is to double-click OrbixERP.cmd and choose from
  the menu. It covers starting, stopping, checking, backing up and viewing
  activity - everything most operators ever need.

  Everything is also available as typed commands, run from the folder you
  installed into:

    Linux / macOS            Windows
    -----------------------  ------------------------
    ./orbixerp.sh <command>  .\orbixerp.ps1 <command>

  This guide writes orbixerp <command> for both. Anything below that has no
  menu entry - restoring a backup, updating, switching database mode - has to
  be typed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The commands
============

  Command: orbixerp start
  What it does: Starts everything and waits until it is genuinely ready

  Command: orbixerp stop
  What it does: Shuts down cleanly. Your data is kept.

  Command: orbixerp restart
  What it does: Stop then start - use after editing .env

  Command: orbixerp status
  What it does: Whether it is running, healthy, and on which address

  Command: orbixerp logs
  What it does: The last 200 lines of application log

  Command: orbixerp backup
  What it does: Writes a database backup into backups/ - one runs
      automatically every night, so this is for taking an extra one

  Command: orbixerp restore <file>
  What it does: Replaces the database from a backup

  Command: orbixerp update <folder>
  What it does: Upgrades to a newer release

  Command: orbixerp version
  What it does: What is installed

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Backups
=======

It is already set up
--------------------

  The installer schedules a backup every night at 02:00. You do not have to
  arrange it, and you should not have to remember it. Everything in this
  section is about checking that it is working and knowing what to do when you
  need it.

  To change the time, or to turn it off, see Changing the backup schedule
  below.

Checking it is running - do this monthly
----------------------------------------

  A schedule that stopped running six weeks ago looks exactly like one that is
  working, until the day you need it. Two things to look at:

  1. Are there recent files?

      ls -lh backups/           # Linux / macOS
      dir backups\              # Windows

  You should see a orbixerp_<date>_<time>.dump for each of the last several
  days, and the newest one should be from last night.

  2. What does the log say?

  Each scheduled run appends to backups/backup.log. The last entry should end
  with Backup complete. The file is trimmed automatically, so it cannot grow
  without limit.

  On Windows you can also ask Task Scheduler directly:

      Get-ScheduledTaskInfo -TaskPath '\OrbixERP\' -TaskName 'Backup (OrbixERP)' |
        Select-Object LastRunTime, LastTaskResult

  LastTaskResult of 0 means the last run succeeded. Anything else means it did
  not - and that is the only thing that tells "scheduled" apart from
  "working".

Taking one yourself
-------------------

      orbixerp backup

  Writes backups/orbixerp_20260801_143022.dump. Take one before anything you
  would want to undo - a big price change, a stock adjustment, an import.

  If it fails, it says so and deletes the part-written file, so a broken
  backup can never be mistaken for a good one. It also refuses to start at all
  if the disk is too full to finish safely.

How long backups are kept
-------------------------

  Three different kinds of file end up in backups/, and they are deliberately
  kept for three different lengths of time:

  File: orbixerp_...
  Taken by: the nightly schedule, and orbixerp backup
  Kept for: 14 days
  Setting: ERP_BACKUP_RETAIN_DAYS

  File: orbixerp-preupdate_...
  Taken by: orbixerp update, before it upgrades
  Kept for: 90 days
  Setting: ERP_BACKUP_PREUPDATE_RETAIN_DAYS

  File: safety-before-restore-...
  Taken by: orbixerp restore, before it overwrites
  Kept for: 30 days
  Setting: ERP_BACKUP_SAFETY_RETAIN_DAYS

  The pre-update file is kept longest on purpose: it is the only way to undo
  an upgrade (see Going back), and a fortnight is not long enough to be
  confident in a new version.

  Underneath those, three limits stop the folder from either emptying itself
  or filling the disk:

  Setting: ERP_BACKUP_KEEP_MIN
  Default: 7
  What it does: Always keep this many of the newest, whatever their age.
      Checked first; it always wins

  Setting: ERP_BACKUP_KEEP_MAX
  Default: 90
  What it does: Never keep more files than this

  Setting: ERP_BACKUP_DIR_MAX_MB
  Default: 2048
  What it does: Never let backups/ grow past this many megabytes

  KEEP_MIN is what stops a machine that was switched off for a month from
  deleting every backup it has the next time it takes one. The two ceilings
  only ever bind on a very small disk or a very large database; when they do,
  the oldest files go first - including, if it comes to it, a pre-update file.
  If you have a rollback you must not lose, copy it somewhere else, which you
  should be doing anyway.

Three things to keep together
-----------------------------

  A database backup on its own is not enough to recover. Keep all three:

            Why
  --------  ----------------------------------
  backups/  your data
  .env      settings and the database password
  secrets/  the sign-in security keys

  Without secrets/, a restored system cannot validate anyone's sign-in and
  every user is logged out. Without .env, the application cannot open its own
  database.

Getting them off the machine - this part is still yours
-------------------------------------------------------

  The schedule writes backups to this machine's own disk. Nothing copies them
  off it. A backup that only exists on the computer that failed is not a
  backup - it is the same disk, the same power supply, the same room, and the
  same fire.

  Arrange one of these, and check it as often as you check the backups
  themselves:

  - a scheduled copy of backups/, .env and secrets/ to another computer or a
    NAS
  - a cloud sync folder or object storage
  - an external drive that is physically taken away, rotated between at least
    two

  > If your OrbixERP is a shared instance - one system used by more than one
    organisation - do not do this yourself. See When the system is shared by
    more than one organisation.

Changing the backup schedule
----------------------------

  Change the time - run the installer again with the time you want. It
  replaces the existing schedule rather than adding a second one, and it does
  not reinstall anything:

      ./install.sh --backup-time 03:30              # Linux / macOS
      .\install.ps1 -BackupTime 03:30               # Windows

  Turn it off - --no-schedule / -NoSchedule on the same command. Only do this
  if something else is backing the database up.

  See it - crontab -l on Linux; on Windows, Task Scheduler -> Task Scheduler
  Library -> OrbixERP.

  Change how long backups are kept - edit the settings in .env (table above).
  No restart is needed; the next backup uses the new values.

  Two things worth knowing about the schedule:

  - On Linux the backup runs through the running system, so it is skipped on
    any night the machine is off or OrbixERP is stopped. It does not queue.
  - On Windows the task runs as the person who installed, and only while that
    person is signed in with Docker Desktop running - which is what a
    back-office or till PC is doing anyway. If Windows refused to create the
    task during installation (it often will not let a standard user), the
    installer says so and prints exactly what to do; see TROUBLESHOOTING.txt.

Restoring
---------

      orbixerp restore backups/orbixerp_20260801_143022.dump

  This replaces the current database. Everything recorded since that backup is
  lost, so the command makes you type RESTORE to confirm. Add --yes (Linux) or
  -Yes (Windows) only when a script is driving it and there is nobody to type.

  Before it overwrites anything it takes a safety-before-restore-... copy of
  the database as it is right now, so a restore of the wrong file can itself
  be undone.

  Practise this once, on purpose, before you ever need it. A backup you have
  never restored is an assumption, and the middle of an emergency is the wrong
  time to find out how long it takes. Your supplier can give you the written
  drill - it is docs/ops/restore-drill.txt in the OrbixERP source - and the
  measured time it took there.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Updating
========

  OrbixERP is released regularly, so you will do this more often than you
  installed it.

  You will be sent a new bundle, e.g. orbixerp-1.2.0-amd64.zip. Unzip it
  somewhere temporary
  - not over your installation folder.

Windows - double-click
----------------------

  Double-click Setup.cmd in the new bundle and point it at your existing
  installation. It recognises what is already there:

  > Version 1.1.0 is already installed in C:\OrbixERP. This bundle is version
    1.2.0. Update the existing installation to 1.2.0?

  Say yes, review what it tells you, and click Update. It skips all the setup
  questions - your database, organisation and network settings are already
  configured and are not asked again.

  It will not let you install fresh over a working system, and if the two
  versions match it simply says there is nothing to do.

Linux / macOS, or from a terminal
---------------------------------

      orbixerp update /path/to/orbixerp-1.2.0-amd64

What an update does, either way
-------------------------------

  Both routes run the same steps - the wizard simply presses the same buttons
  for you:

  1. Check the release matches your machine's processor type
  2. Take a backup of your database - and stop entirely if that backup fails
  3. Load the new software
  4. Refresh the configuration files, guides and shortcuts
  5. Record the new version, restart, and wait until the system is genuinely
     healthy
  6. Tell you the name of the backup from step 2

What is kept, and what is replaced
----------------------------------

  Kept, untouched                         Replaced with the new version
  --------------------------------------  ---------------------------------
  Your data - the whole database          The application itself
  .env - all your settings and passwords  The docker-compose files
  secrets/ - your signing keys            The guides in docs/
  backups/ - every existing backup        The scripts and Windows shortcuts

  Nobody has to sign in again, and nothing has to be reconfigured.

Going back
----------

  > Read this before updating. Database changes only run forwards. Once a new
    version has upgraded your database, the previous version will not start
    against it. Putting the old software back does not undo an update.
  > The only way back is to restore the backup taken in step 2. The update
    prints its exact filename - keep it until you are satisfied the new
    version is behaving.

      orbixerp restore backups/orbixerp_<the-one-it-named>.dump

  Then reinstall the previous bundle.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Giving it a proper web address
==============================

  Straight after installation people reach OrbixERP at the computer's own name
  and a port:

      http://SERVER-PC:8080

  That works on your office network immediately. The steps below make it
  nicer, and you can stop at whichever one is enough for you.

1. Stop the address changing - give the computer a fixed IP
-----------------------------------------------------------

  If the machine gets its address automatically, that address can change after
  a power cut and everyone's bookmarks break. Ask whoever manages your router
  or network for a DHCP reservation (sometimes called a static lease) for this
  computer. Nothing changes in OrbixERP.

2. Reach it by a name you choose - http://erp.mycompany.local:8080
------------------------------------------------------------------

  Add one entry to your internal DNS - on a Windows domain controller, your
  router, or your firewall - pointing a name at that fixed IP:

      erp.mycompany.local   ->   192.168.1.50

  Nothing changes in OrbixERP. This is purely a network change.

3. Drop the port number - http://erp.mycompany.local
----------------------------------------------------

  Set the port to 80 in .env, then orbixerp restart:

      ERP_HTTP_PORT=80

  > Port 80 is often already taken on Windows, by IIS or another web
    application. If the system then refuses to start, that is why - put the
    port back and use option 2.

4. A real internet address with HTTPS - https://erp.mycompany.com
-----------------------------------------------------------------

  You need a domain you own, with its DNS pointing at this machine, and ports
  80 and 443 reachable. Then see Turning on HTTPS below - you get a proper
  trusted certificate automatically and for free.

A folder on an existing website is NOT supported
------------------------------------------------

  An address like https://mycompany.com/orbix-erp - OrbixERP living in a
  folder beneath a site you already run - does not work, and pointing a proxy
  at it will produce a blank page. The web client is built to load from the
  root of whatever address serves it.

  Give it its own name instead, which is the normal way to do this and needs
  no special setup:

          https://mycompany.com/orbix-erp     will not work
          https://erp.mycompany.com           correct - a subdomain of the same domain

  A subdomain costs nothing, is one DNS entry, and can point at a completely
  different machine from your main website. If a folder-style address is a
  firm requirement for your organisation, talk to your supplier - it is
  possible, but it is a change to the software rather than a setting.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Turning on HTTPS
================

  By default the system is served over plain http on your local network. That
  is normally fine on a trusted office network. Turn on encryption if it is
  reachable more widely, or if your policies require it.

  In .env:

      ERP_TLS_ENABLED=true
      ERP_PUBLIC_HOST=erp.mycompany.co.tz     # the name or IP users type
      ERP_BIND_ADDR=127.0.0.1                 # stop the unencrypted port being reachable

  Then orbixerp restart.

  With an IP address or an internal name, the certificate is self-signed:
  traffic is encrypted, but browsers warn that the site is "not private" and
  users must click through.

  > Do not stop there - clicking through is not a solution. A self-signed
    setup issues itself a fresh certificate every 12 hours, and "proceed
    anyway" only ever applied to the one it replaced. Twice a day, users find
    the page still opens (from cache) while everything they do fails,
    typically appearing as "Sign-in failed. Please try again." See
    TROUBLESHOOTING.txt.
  > If you are staying on a self-signed certificate, install the certificate
    authority on every computer that uses the system, once:
      docker exec orbixerp-caddy cat /data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt > orbixerp-ca.crt
  > Install orbixerp-ca.crt under Trusted Root Certification Authorities on
    each PC. That authority is long-lived, so every future certificate is
    trusted automatically and the warnings stop for good.

  With a real domain name whose DNS points at this machine, and ports 80 and
  443 reachable from the internet, you get a proper trusted certificate free:
  delete the line tls internal from Caddyfile and run orbixerp restart.
  Renewal is automatic from then on. This is the better answer - no
  certificate to install on anyone's machine.

  > A cloud provider's own hostname will not work for this. Addresses such as
    ec2-...compute.amazonaws.com are refused by the free certificate
    authority. You need a domain you own.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Changing settings
=================

  Edit .env, then orbixerp restart.

  Commonly changed:

  Setting: ERP_HTTP_PORT
  Meaning: The port users browse to

  Setting: ERP_BIND_ADDR
  Meaning: 0.0.0.0 for network access, 127.0.0.1 for this machine only

  Setting: ERP_TIME_ZONE
  Meaning: Timezone for displayed dates and times

  Setting: ERP_BACKUP_RETAIN_DAYS
  Meaning: How long nightly backups are kept - see How long backups are kept

  Setting: JAVA_OPTS
  Meaning: Memory tuning - raise only if you also gave Docker more memory

  Changing the time the nightly backup runs is not a .env setting - see
  Changing the backup schedule.

  Settings whose names start with ERP_BOOTSTRAP_ are read only when the
  database is first created. Changing them later has no effect; use the
  application's own screens.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When the system is shared by more than one organisation
=======================================================

  Some OrbixERP installations are shared: one system, one database, used by
  more than one organisation, kept apart inside the application. If yours is
  one of those - your supplier will have told you - this section replaces the
  backup advice above, and it is not optional.

One backup file holds every organisation's data
-----------------------------------------------

  A backup is a copy of the whole database. It is not "your data" - it is
  every organisation on that system: their sales, their customers, their
  prices, their payroll. There is no per-organisation backup, and no way to
  take one.

  Two things follow, and they are the whole of it:

  1. You cannot take, hold or restore a backup of a shared system. Not to a
  USB drive, not to your own cloud storage, not to your IT provider. A copy of
  that folder is a copy of another organisation's books, and handing it on
  would be a data-protection incident whatever the intention.

  2. Backups are your supplier's responsibility, and they should have told you
  in writing what they do and what you are entitled to expect:

  - how often a backup is taken, and how much work you could lose (your RPO)
  - how long it takes to get you running again (your RTO), measured, not
    estimated
  - where backups are held, for how long, and who can read them
  - who is told, and how, when a restore happens

  If you do not have those four answers, ask for them. They are the service,
  not the software.

A restore affects everybody, so it is never a routine request
-------------------------------------------------------------

  Restoring goes back to the moment the backup was taken for every
  organisation on the system, not just the one that asked. Another
  organisation's day of trading disappears, and the invoice numbers they
  already issued get issued again.

  So on a shared system a restore is a decision your supplier makes, with
  everyone affected told beforehand - not something you can ask for as a
  matter of course. If you have lost data, say so immediately; there are often
  ways to put a specific mistake right that do not involve rolling the whole
  system backwards.

Nobody outside your supplier gets access to the machine
-------------------------------------------------------

  The installation folder holds the backups, the database password and the
  sign-in keys for everyone using the system. Access to the machine, that
  folder, or those files is limited to your supplier's named staff - which
  means an IT provider working for one organisation cannot be given it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Moving to a different machine
=============================

  1. On the old machine: orbixerp backup, then orbixerp stop - in that order.
     The backup reads the database through the running system, so it cannot
     run once you have stopped it
  2. Copy the whole installation folder - including backups/, .env and
     secrets/
  3. On the new machine: install Docker, then run the installer. It finds the
     existing .env and keeps your settings and keys
  4. orbixerp restore backups/<the newest file>

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Running a second instance (e.g. a training system)
==================================================

  You can run a separate instance on the same machine - useful for training
  staff, or trying something out without touching live data.

  1. Unzip the bundle again into a different folder, e.g. C:\OrbixERP-Training
  2. Run the installer there, and when it finishes, edit that folder's .env:
         ERP_STACK_NAME=orbixerp-training     # must differ from the live one
         ERP_HTTP_PORT=8081              # must differ from the live one
  3. orbixerp restart in that folder

  The two keep entirely separate databases, containers and backups. Nothing
  you do in the training instance can affect the live one.

  > Never change ERP_STACK_NAME on an existing installation. It is the name of
    the volume holding your data. Changing it makes the system start against a
    fresh, empty database, and it will look exactly as though everything has
    been lost.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Switching between "docker" and "host" database mode
===================================================

  1. orbixerp backup
  2. Prepare the destination - for host, follow HOST-DB-SETUP.txt
  3. Change ERP_DB_MODE in .env (and the connection details, if moving to
     host)
  4. orbixerp start, let it create the empty structure, then orbixerp restore
     backups/<file>

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Where things are stored
=======================

  Your data
  docker mode: Docker volume orbixerp-db-data on this machine
  host mode: On your own PostgreSQL server

  Backups
  docker mode: backups/
  host mode: backups/

  Settings
  docker mode: .env
  host mode: .env

  Security keys
  docker mode: secrets/jwt/
  host mode: secrets/jwt/

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Two things never to do
======================

  Never run docker compose down -v. The -v deletes the database volume and
  everything in it. orbixerp stop is always the safe shutdown.

  Never delete the orbixerp-db-data volume in Docker Desktop's interface. In
  docker mode, that volume is your database.
